To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corticosteroid resistance is associated with increased expression of c-fos in T cells and monocytes.
c-fos synthesis is increased in the monocytes and T cells of corticosteroid- resistant asthmatic patients and this increased c-fos is associated with decreased GR-DNA binding in these cells.
c-fos expression is increased in PBMCs and their subpopulations from CR but not CS asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of c-fos in the pathogenesis of corticosteroid resistance.
a novel mechanism for corticosteroid resistance in asthma, namely the generation of c-Fos.
the molecular mechanisms that contribute to glucocorticoid insensitivity in asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcription rate, mRNA levels, and protein expression of c-fos are significantly greater in CR asthma than in CS asthma, and that this may be a key mechanism underlying corticosteroid resistance in this disease.
the increased c-Fos expression in the PBMCs from the CR asthmatics is a result of the increased transcription rate and not due to any increased stability of the c-Fos mRNA.
the increased expression of c-fos in CR asthmatic patients is associated with increased AP-1 and decreased GR DNA-binding activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
increased c-f os synthesis provides a major explanation for the corticosteroid resistance observed in a subset of asthmatics.
increased c-foss synthesis is a major mechanism for corticosteroid resistance in bronchial asthma.

the increased c-fos transcriptional rate, mRNA and c-fos protein levels in CR asthma may provide a major mechanism for increased AP-1 DNA binding activity and decreased GR DNA binding activity in CR asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
c-fos is an important mediator of the corticosteroid resistant phenotype in asthma and that c-fos antisens may provide a novel therapeutic approach for corticosteroid resistance.
c-Fos is a key factor in the development of corticosteroid resistance in bronchial asthma and may provide a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of this disorder.
c-fos is a key regulator of the corticosteroid response in asthma.
